nature-nurture.def: The question of how heredity (nature) and environment and experience (nurture) contribute to behavior and mental processes. Psychologists now study how the two interact rather than which one wins.

heredity.def: The passing of traits and tendencies from biological parents to their children.

heritability.def: The proportion of the variation in a trait, within a particular group and environment, that is linked to genetic differences. It does not apply to one person and can change when the environment changes.

evolutionary-psychology.def: The study of how behavior and mental processes may have been shaped by natural selection because they helped our ancestors survive and reproduce.

natural-selection.def: The process by which inherited traits that help an organism survive and reproduce are passed on more often, becoming more common over generations.

eugenics.def: A discredited movement, begun in the late 1800s, that tried to "improve" humanity by controlling who could have children; it led to forced sterilization and, in Nazi Germany, mass murder.

twin-study.def: A study that compares how alike identical twins (who share all their genes) and fraternal twins (who share about half) are on a trait, to estimate genetic influence.

adoption-study.def: A study that compares adopted children with their biological parents (shared genes) and their adoptive parents (shared environment).

family-study.def: A study of how often a trait appears among relatives of different closeness, to see whether it runs in families.
